messages.subject: Debugging IO exception
parts:
I've been making use of the reduce phase, but there's just one hitch I
can't seem to figure out. In my map phase, I call rhcollect(ix,
Mval). The Mval is a list with multiple components, one of which is
another list, and inside that is one element with a 100x100 matrix.

When the reducer receives this object, it fails, with the error below
appearing in the Hadoop logs:

java.io.IOException: subprocess still running
::MROutput/MRErrThread failed:java.lang.RuntimeException:
R ERROR BEGIN (reduce.setup):


I've managed to get things through if I reduce the matrix to 50x50.
I've also experimented with just the matrix, and have had crashes b/c
of the heap size; by increasing the heap size, I can get much larger
individual matrices to the reducer, e.g. 5000x5000, by setting the
Java heap size to be sufficiently large (i.e. with
mapred.child.java.opts = "-Xmx2500m").

In any case, the errors are also different - if I use this nested
object, it crashes with the error above; a simple matrix crashes with
a Java heap size error. Since the above message is really about IO
and not heap sizes, I looked at changing the io.sort.mb option, but
that doesn't seem to help.

Is there something else that could cause this to crash?

Thanks,

David

parts:
For a given key how many values does the reducer receive? You can decrease
the umber using rhipe_reduce_buffer_size (default is 6000)

Note, a 100x100 matrix inside a list is 80KB , e.g.

length(rhsz(list(runif(10),matrix(runif(100*100),ncol=100))))

Reproducible code would be helpful.

Regards
J

messages.author: 76174213f7be4102
messages.subject: Re: Debugging IO exception
parts:
I think I may have solved this.

To follow up: in the smallest case, there are just 2 values. After
reading your suggestion, I tried just 1 value, but that also created
problems. You're right about the size - it's also countable as 8 byte
double floats, with 10K entries. In the 50x50 case, this is just 20K.

Creating a reproducible example is hard - my code and data depend on
things that are local. The tests of 50x50 (worked) and 100x100
(didn't work) are reproducible in my setup.

However, there's a notable package that is getting loaded in my setup:
bigmemory. I changed from "setup = setup" to "setup = list(map =
map.setup)", and loaded bigmemory only in the map stage. This seems
to have resolved the issue. I wonder if the issue is that the reducer
was not responding, because it was loading a package. If so, then
that would explain my difficulty in making reproducible examples -
everything omitted the loading of the bigmemory package.

By the way, bigmemory may send the package loading message to STDERR,
rather than STDOUT, as it's one of the only packages that produces an
"error" when loaded while running Rhipe, while other packages'
messages do not appear in the logs.

I'll post again if I can develop a concise example. However, it seems
to be resolved for me.

Thanks!

David

parts:
This seems to do the trick. Although bigmemory isn't used in this
case, its use creates the problem in the reduce step. If I did want
to use bigmemory in the reduce phase, how would I load it so that it
doesn't create problems?

____

setup <- expression({
library(bigmemory)
})

map <- expression({
lapply(seq_along(map.values),
function(r){
tmpVal = matrix(rnorm(10000), ncol = 100)
rhcollect(1, tmpVal)
})
})

reduce <- expression(
reduce = { results = reduce.values },
post = { rhcollect(1, results) }
)

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Debugging IO exception
parts:
I'm surprised that that code worked.

This is my code

library(Rhipe)
rhinit()
rhoptions(runner=sprintf("%s/rhipe.runner.sh",Sys.getenv("HOME")))
options(width=300)


setup <- expression({
library(bigmemory,lib.loc="/home/ba01/u132/sguha/R_LIBS")
})
map <- expression({
lapply(map.values, function(r) rhcollect(1,2))
})
reduce=expression(
reduce={
rhcollect(1L, reduce.values)
})
z <- rhmr(map=map,reduce=reduce, N=10,
setup=setup,inout=c("lapply","sequence"),ofolder="/wsc/tmp/sg2",mapred=list(mapred.map.tasks=2,mapred.reduce.tasks=2))
rhex(z)

(you ought to skip then rhoptions statement at the beginning).

Anyways, on running this

R ERROR BEGIN (map.setup):
=============


bigmemory >= 4.0 is a major revision since 3.1.2; please see package
biganalytics and http://www.bigmemory.org for more information.


R ERROR END
===========


Now if i wrap library in as

setup <- expression({
suppressMessages(library(bigmemory,lib.loc="/home/ba01/u132/sguha//R_LIBS"))
})

It works.

Notice the bigmemory is in both the map and reduce.

Also, if you use a combiner, the setup is never called for the reducer
when it is combining but is called when reducing. The variable
.rhipe.current.state (yes '.' is a prefix) is 'map.combine' when the
reducer code is being called asa combiner.

Cheers
S

(Currently, if you have millions of keys and /few/ values per key, the
reducer can crawl. I'm trying to fix this which will require a
slightly different semantic. R execution is pathetic if a function is
called repeatedly, best to call once with many values.)

On May 5, 8:12 pm, Saptarshi Guha <saptarshi.g...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I'm surprised that that code worked.

I think there may be a misunderstanding. To clarify: without a reduce
phase (let's call it "experiment 1": just drop the reducer), the code
will work, and the following "error" message has no impact:

R ERROR BEGIN (map.setup):
=============

bigmemory >= 4.0 is a major revision since 3.1.2; please see package
biganalytics and http://www.bigmemory.org for more information.

R ERROR END
===========

That message is, I think, indicative of bigmemory using STDERR. If
you load the package from a regular R console, you get the same
message. So, I think that bigmemory sends messages to STDERR or some
other destination, which Rhipe picks up & then sends to the error
logs.

However, the other issue that arises is that the code sample I gave
*doesn't* work ("experiment 2"). :) On my setup, if the
rnorm(100000),ncol(100) is changed to, say, rnorm(100),ncol(10), then
the reduce phase works ("experiment 3"). For the example I gave, the
reduce phase fails, with this additional error (beyond the "error" of
bigmemory):

Because the system may or may not be affected by hardware, you may
need to tweak the scale a little. I've seen it work at 10x10 and
50x50 matrices, and fail at 100x100, and, for kicks, I tested up to
5000x5000. But, for another system, it may fail at 50x50 or be fine
for larger scales. I suspect the key is the IO exception message, but
I'm not sure what subprocess is referenced.

Suppressing messages is an interesting idea. I tried experiment 2,
with 100x100 matrices, and it succeeds. It's possible that the IO
message is a redherring and that the output from bigmemory is
problematic after all. However, it's not the error per se (because
smaller scale matrices can still work), but something else. In any
case, its output notice is unnecessary when run remotely, so I'll
suppress its loading message.

Thanks!

David
